reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible professor. Will work with you whether you have questions about the actual course/work or will be understanding about any personal matters you have going on. Couldn't recommend him for any courses you are taking at A&M.

Every time I have the opportunity to take a class with him I try to incorporate it in my schedule if possible. ML is a difficult subject but Prof makes sure to explain in heavy detail and answer any questions you may have to make sure that you thoroughly understand the concepts as well as possible. Absolutely great lecturer and person all around!

I took this as a summer course, so information was dense. That said, even while working full time, the course was paced in a way that didn't feel overwhelming or impossible to keep up with. There were about 7 very manageable HWs, and very accessible office hours if you needed help. The exams were similar to the practice, and the final was kind :).

Although the content was difficult, Professor Duysak made the course extremely manageable. He'd give out plenty of extensions and offer bonus points on tests with bonus questions. He is super nice, caring, and lenient. I'd definitely take him again!

I took him for 441 for some reason his class course doesn't show up but I took CSCE 441. His teachings were very well if you didn't understand the concept he'd gladly come and help you understand key points of the topic, class was very easy and he's a very lenient grader as well given extensions of needed
Best professor I have had in all of my college years thus far.

Dr. Duysak is an incredible professor. He's passionate about teaching, always willing to work with you, shifts deadlines, even let my buddy take an exam that he slept through. I had him for many courses, and  can confirm that he is a certified goated professor. He even brought baklava to class one time! Solid lecturer as well.

He's truly an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and is always available to answer questions. I had him for a summer course and even though it was extremely fast-paced, he made sure we stayed on track, made homework assignments very doable and constantly updated his lectures. You should take him if he teaches the course!

His lectures can get boring but it is just the nature of the course. HW is challenging if you don't keep up with it and will only get more so later in the semester homework so make sure you seek resources for help. Alpaslan genuinely cares and will often be lenient with deadlines compared to other 120 profs. Super chill dude.

Professor Duysak is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students and having them learn. He encourages you to ask questions if you are not sure about something. He is also very understanding and allows you to take extensions for assignments as needed because he understands we have a life outside of school. My favorite professor thus far!

I thoroughly enjoyed this class, and think that it was taught very well by Mr. Duysak. His lectures were very informative and he prepared us very well for the exams. He is very caring for his students and actively engages with them throughout his lectures to ensure that they understand the material.

Dr. Alpaslan truly cares for his students and tries his best to ensure that we grasp the concepts he covers. During in-class lectures, he regularly asks whether or not his teaching methods help us and how he can improve. I can say without doubt that his way of teaching and presenting helped me hone my coding skills.
Made everything very easy to understand and cares for his students. Most homeworks were well made and a good challenge. Be weary of second exam

Professor Alpaslan is the best professor, He cares a lot about his students and always there for help whenever you need it. The class powerpoints has everything you need to learn about the subject. Even If you don't understand something you just need to ask him and he explain it in best way possible. I would definitely take him again.

He was a good prof and interactive in lecture. There are about 10 coding assignments (sometimes mini reports) which he was flexible on the due dates for if the class was having difficulty, and 2 midterms and a final. The exams were a little tough and long, but he made reviews and went over content before each test so it was manageable to study.
Pretty solid professor. Very hands off and learn at your own pace. Tests make sense and homeworks are clear.

The course material is tough, but Dr. Duysak did his best to ensure we stayed on track. The class is graded through homeworks and exams -- the homeworks are usually coding assignments or reports in Python, and the exams always had review materials. Overall, I enjoyed my time in the class, especially due to Dr. Duysak's willingness to help.

A very good person. Since it was his first time teaching, the HWs had a few errors, but he would always fix those as quickly as possible and provide extensions on the HWs.
His exam reviews helped a lot in the exams. He would put examples on those reviews similar to the exams.
Very active and accessible outside of class. Class was also interesting.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A solid professor for the CSCE120 class! Alpaslan was always able to answer questions when asked in a way that deeply furthered understanding of the topic at hand and his notes were very detailed and descriptive. Gave out excellent exams reviews that would help for the test and always gave opportunities to improve oneself given you put in the work.

A really good professor, if you have any difficulty all you have to do is reach out to him - I think it was because his classes were online that some people did not like his class but personally I really liked his class and when you take the time to review the slides it makes a lot of sense and is very intuitive to follow.

To be honest, I really wish that I could give this professor a higher rating. He is a super nice guy and you can tell he is really trying his hardest. With that being said, the course was a mess. Due dates being moved around all the time, no communication, first midterm took a month to be graded, the list goes on. I do not recommend taking him.

he's a really nice guy and very communicative and open to feedback 
however class was definitely not organized as he would constantly move deadlines due to seemingly not taking account homework difficulty or due to autograder problems; the slides and material provided were not accurate or very good either

"disorganized" is putting it lightly. The tests were ridiculously hard on an insane time restriction. He posted review questions with incorrect solutions. The homework used an autograder that never worked. None of the slides look like they took more than 30 seconds to make. He is a nice guy but this class is a disaster.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Records all lectures but does not give them to anyone.

He makes you swap the order of variables returned from functions in libraries because he feels like it, forces you to not use the dataset properly so your accuracy drops from 90% to 70%, and the data given doesn't have headers like the ones in gradescope.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Alpaslan's notes were very very detailed so as long as you go through them and spend time reading them you will be fine. The exams we're incredibly easy and very closely followed the material.

I really wanted to like this class but it has been awful. It has been catastrophically disorganized and needlessly confusing/difficult. The lectures often had incorrect notation/equations. The homework's autograder had no leniency for any slight mistakes, so they had to give us the working code several times (also unclear instructions). AVOID!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework
